root_cause.text: The vulnerability stems from the `dualshock4_parse_report` function in the HID PlayStation driver using the unvalidated `num_touch_reports` field from the device as a loop bound without checking it against the `touch_reports` array size, resulting in an out-of-bounds memory read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "the loop in dualshock4_parse_report will read off the end of the touch_reports array" if the device lies about the count, and the patch diff shows the fix applying `min_t(u8, ..., ARRAY_SIZE(...))` to both USB and Bluetooth report parsing paths to clamp the value to the maximum array size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Bounds the touch report count to the array size to prevent potential buffer overflow
intent_record.what: Replaced direct assignment of bt->num_touch_reports with a min_t operation capping the value against ARRAY_SIZE(bt->touch_reports)
intent_record.how: Prevents num_touch_reports from exceeding the physical capacity of the touch_reports array, mitigating potential out-of-bounds memory access risks
